```{r}
library(data.table)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(car) # Required for Type II ANOVA 

# How much of the variation in energy usage can each predictor (Occupancy and Entrances) explain? 
# Type1 Anova is sequential which will lead statistical conclusions to change depending on order variables are written in the code 
# Type 2: Does this variable explain anything after accounting for all the other predictors? i.e. comparing energy ~ entrances, with energy ~ entrances + avg_occupancy
```

```{r}
occupancy <- read_csv("OccupantData/OccupancyLog_05202026.csv")
energy_wide <- read_csv("Analysis/ENERGY_20052026.csv")
```

```{r}
# as energy_wide contains NA - only logs values for state changes, 
# converts the lgl (all NA) columns to dbl NA, matching real numeric columns
energy_long <- energy_wide %>%
  mutate(across(-c(entity_id, type, unit), as.numeric)) %>%
  pivot_longer( # pivot from wide to long; each timestamp column becomes row
    cols = -c(entity_id, type, unit),
    names_to = "timestamp",
    values_to = "energy_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(timestamp = as.POSIXct(timestamp, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OSZ", tz = "UTC"))

# forward AND backward fill per entity to completely eliminate structural NAs
energy_long <- energy_long %>%
  arrange(entity_id, timestamp) %>%
  group_by(entity_id) %>%
  fill(energy_value, .direction = "downup") %>% 
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
energy_dt <- as.data.table(energy_long)
occupancy_dt <- as.data.table(occupancy)

# preserve original timestamps under new names before joining as join will overwrite/consume originals
energy_dt[, energy_timestamp := timestamp]
occupancy_dt[, occ_timestamp := timestamp_start]

setkey(energy_dt, timestamp)
setkey(occupancy_dt, timestamp_start)

# as occupancy sensors record data in 1 minute intervals, while smart plugs record energy every 15 minutes; time stamps listed do not match 
# forward-fill join / rolling join: if no exact match, use last known occupancy reading forward
joined_data <- occupancy_dt[energy_dt, roll = TRUE, on = c("timestamp_start" = "timestamp")]

# check match quality
names(joined_data)
```

```{r}
# time_diff states absolute time gap in minutes between energy reading and occupancy reading that got rolled onto it
joined_data[, time_diff := abs(as.numeric(difftime(timestamp_start, energy_timestamp, units = "mins")))]

sum(is.na(joined_data$avg_occupancy)) # how many energy rows failed to match any occupancy record at all 
```

```{r}
joined_data_clean <- joined_data%>% 
  filter(time_diff <= 60)  # keep only matches where occupancy is less than 60 minutes 
```

```{r}
nrow(joined_data_clean)
```

```{r}
nrow(joined_data)
```

```{r}
# checking no remaining NAs 
joined_data_clean %>%
  group_by(entity_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_energy_na = sum(is.na(energy_value)),
    n_occ_na = sum(is.na(avg_occupancy))
  )
```

```{r}
# regression-based ANOVA decomposition

# occupancy_sensitivity_pct — partial eta-squared for avg_occupancy, as a %. 
  # "of this appliance's energy variance, what fraction is uniquely attributable to occupancy, after accounting for entrances."
# standardized_slope — direction and relative strength, in standard-deviation units (not kWh). 
    # Positive = energy increases when occupancy rises; negative = energy decreases when occupancy rises.
# total_r_squared — how much of the appliance's total energy variance is explained by the whole model (occupancy + entrances together) 

compute_sensitivity <- function(df) {
  has_traffic_variation <- sd(df$entrances) > 0 # checks first whether entrances varies (not just 0 for whole data)

  tryCatch({
    # if entrances varies, fit a two-predictor model (avg_occupancy + entrances) and use Type II ANOVA to partition variances 
    if (has_traffic_variation) {
      fit <- lm(scale(energy_value) ~ scale(avg_occupancy) + scale(entrances), data = df) 
        # standardizes each variable (mean0, sd1) before regression - allows to compare appliances with very different energy scales
      anova_df <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(fit, type = "II"))
    # if entrances doesn't vary, Type 1 anova()
    } else {
      fit <- lm(scale(energy_value) ~ scale(avg_occupancy), data = df)
      anova_df <- as.data.frame(anova(fit))
    }

    ss_occupancy <- anova_df["scale(avg_occupancy)", "Sum Sq"]
    ss_residuals <- anova_df["Residuals", "Sum Sq"]

    tibble(
      n = nrow(df),
      occupancy_sensitivity_pct = (ss_occupancy / (ss_occupancy + ss_residuals)) * 100, # measures how sensitive energy is to occupancy once entrances are alr accounted for
      standardized_slope        = coef(fit)[["scale(avg_occupancy)"]], # Energy = β0 + β1 × Occupancy, where β1 means if occupancy increases by 1 person, energy changes by β1 watts
        # since occupancy standardised, z = x − μ / σ; 1 unit = 1 sd; where x = Occupancy, mu = average occupancy, sd = 2 people 
      total_r_squared           = summary(fit)$r.squared
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    tibble(n = nrow(df), occupancy_sensitivity_pct = NA_real_,
           standardized_slope = NA_real_, total_r_squared = NA_real_)
  })
}
```

```{r}
sensitivity_global <- joined_data_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(energy_value), !is.na(avg_occupancy), !is.na(entrances)) %>%
  group_by(entity_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 30, sd(energy_value) > 0, sd(avg_occupancy) > 0) %>% # filters out appliances where zero variance in energy or occupancy
  group_modify(~ compute_sensitivity(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(occupancy_sensitivity_pct)) %>%
  arrange(desc(occupancy_sensitivity_pct))
```

```{r}
print(sensitivity_global)
# identify occupancy-sensitive appliances with: 
# high occupancy_sensitivity_pct, positive standardized_slope, and a small total_r_squared − occupancy_sensitivity_pct/100 gap
```
